findings.observed: Extrapolation uses per-candidate rate measured at 8000 candidates; actual extended-budget CPU differs materially from training+inference+neural search. Archived per-seed baseline difference is -21.0%, -8.3%, and +18.4% versus model CPU.
findings.reproduction: In selector.py run_seed, extra=int(rate*(train_cpu_seconds+inference)/len(goals)); compare out[all_concepts_equal_total_cpu].cpu_seconds alone, NOT add the separate standard all_concepts run, to training+inference+out[model].cpu_seconds. See three_seed_audit.
findings.required_fix: Use measured per-arm CPU matching or calibrated budgets with a prespecified tolerance; rerun the 3 seeds on identical goals; do not infer equality from candidate-rate extrapolation alone.

limitations: All three 30,000-dream training phases reran from pinned code; six of seven comparison arms per seed reran and exactly matched archive. Extended-budget baseline reruns were canceled once independent acceptance failures were established; no new full-budget baseline CPU comparison is claimed.
Five archived positive all-concepts expressions were separately checked exhaustively, not all accepted expressions in every comparison arm.
Held-out split hashes are computed over the fixed sparse 86-by-52 input grid, not all 65536 input pairs.
Only 0-5 of 300 exam functions were solved per arm. NO_GAIN cannot rule out small effects on other exam distributions.
No claim of generally optimal compute path, independent model discovery, or AGI; no champion change.
